I've been farming these 18.4 mu since I was 17—thirty-five years now. Got my agricultural college education back in the day, so I understand the science, but the textbooks don't know my fields like I do. My wife and I are the only ones at home now; she works part-time at the garment factory in town, so I'm handling most of the farm work myself. I split the land into 8 mu of cotton and 10.4 mu of wheat-maize double cropping. Cotton gives better returns when prices are decent, but wheat-maize is my insurance—more mechanized, faster turnover, and I need the grain for household security.

**Winter wheat** is already in the ground—I sowed Xinmai 26 last October at about 12 kg/mu and put down 50 kg/mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as basal. Now it's green-up season. I'll irrigate once in late March to break dormancy and activate the basal nutrients. At jointing stage—around mid-April—I'll topdress 18 kg/mu of urea. That brings my total N to about 16 kg/mu, which based on my soil fertility and well water availability should support a yield target of 480 kg/mu. I'll irrigate again at booting if rainfall is below 15 mm that week, and once more at grain filling in mid-May. Last year I skipped the grain-filling irrigation to save 80 yuan on pumping and lost 40 kg/mu—false economy. For pest management, I'll spray a fungicide at flag-leaf stage; powdery mildew has shown up three of the last five years.

**Summer maize** goes in immediately after wheat harvest in early June—sometimes I only have five days between harvest and planting. I'll hire the combine for wheat and drill Zhengdan 958 at 2.5 kg/mu the same day. I'm applying 45 kg/mu of high-nitrogen compound (28-6-6) at planting, which gives me about 12.6 kg N/mu. At the big-trumpet stage, if the lower leaves start yellowing, I'll side-dress another 10 kg/mu of urea—adds about 4.6 kg N/mu. Total N around 17 kg/mu, targeting 520 kg/mu yield. Two irrigations: one at silking and one at grain filling, depending on rain. I'll apply pre-emergence herbicide right after planting; with only two of us I can't afford to weed by hand.

**Cotton** on the 8 mu gets planted mid-to-late April with Lumianyan 37 hybrid seed. Cotton is cash but labor-heavy. Basal fertilizer is 40 kg/mu of compound (15-15-6), and I'll topdress 12 kg/mu of urea at initial flowering. That keeps total N around 11.5 kg/mu—cotton vegetates too much with excess N and delays boll-setting, learned that in 2019. Two irrigations: one at flowering and one at peak boll formation, both furrow irrigation from the well. I'll spray herbicide after planting and watch closely for bollworm in July; if I see eggs I'll hit it with insecticide immediately. Picking is the bottleneck—with just my wife and me, I'll hire pickers at harvest for about 8 labor-days. I'm expecting around 300 kg/mu of seed cotton.

Cash flow matters. Total input costs this season will run about 10,500 yuan. I have the cash, but I'm not pushing rates to the maximum—even if 20 kg N/mu might theoretically add another 20 kg yield, the marginal return doesn't justify the risk if prices drop or drought hits. I'd rather have 2,000 yuan in reserve for medical or machine repair emergencies.
